land.text: Seuthes III's realm round Seuthopolis, sacked by Celts in 281 BC; Tylis lay about 20 km east

predecessors.note: The odrysian-kingdom dossier names tylis as its successor; the Seuthopolis page: 'In 281 BC it was sacked by Celts'.

capitals.name: Tylis (Tulovo)
capitals.note: 'The modern Bulgarian village of Tulovo in Stara Zagora Province now occupies the site.' Coordinates are the researcher's approximation of the village; neither page gives them.

correction.text: eastern Thrace near 'the eastern edge of the Haemus (Balkan) Mountains in what is now eastern Bulgaria', round Tylis (Tulovo)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Tylis. No page opened gives an area, a frontier or a city other than the capital, so the shape is an 80 km disc (about 20,000 km2) round Tulovo, a placeholder for eastern Thrace and a guess at the size of the realm. Whether it reached the Black Sea or the Propontis (the Comontorius page has Byzantium paying tribute) is not on any page. The rendering agent should draw it soft and small.

region.text: eastern Thrace round Tylis, near the eastern edge of the Haemus (Balkan) Mountains

ledger.note: 278: Comontorius founds the kingdom of Tylis. 'Comontorius was a Celtic king in Thrace who in 278 BC founded the kingdom of Tylis.' The Tylis page puts it after the Gauls' defeat by Antigonus Gonatas at Lysimachia in 277 BC 'after which they turned inland to Thrace and founded their kingdom at Tylis'; the Tile Ridge caption on that page says 279-213. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the year is on the page, but no page gives any extent; the 80 km disc is a placeholder]

212: the Thracians destroy Tylis. 'Under Cavarus, Tylis was destroyed by the Thracians in 212 BC' and 'His capital was destroyed by the Thracians in 212 BC and this was also the end of his kingdom' (Tylis page, which also has 213 in a caption). No page names who took the land. [Reviewer eu-02-x, 2026-10-19: confidence 3 to 2: the year is on the page, but no page gives any extent; the 80 km disc is a placeholder]

wars.name: Gallic invasion of the Balkans
belligerents: Celts under Brennus, Bolgios and Cerethrius

zones.text: Thrace, where the survivors settled after 277

wars.outcome: The Gauls overran Thrace and Macedonia, were beaten at Delphi (279) and at Lysimachia by Antigonus II Gonatas (277); the survivors under Comontorius founded a short-lived city-state.
wars.note: Source for the 280 start: 'In 280 BC, a great army comprising about 85,000 warriors left Pannonia'. The Tylis page gives the settlement after 277; the Comontorius page gives 278 for the founding.

certainty.note: No page gives any frontier of Tylis; the disc is a placeholder.

notes: Five pages, all thin on territory: no page opened gives Tylis's area, frontier, cities or kings' reigns, so the shape is an 80 km disc round Tulovo at confidence 3 for the dates and 1 in effect for the extent (the keyframe note says so). Disagreements: founding 278 (Comontorius page) against after 277 (Tylis page) and 279 (Tile Ridge caption); end 212 (text, Comontorius and Cavarus pages) against 213 (caption). Not recorded because no page dates them: Comontorius's tribute from Byzantium ('imposing a tribute on the city of Byzantium', undated; Cavarus 'maintained good relations with the city of Byzantium'), the Thracian revolt that ended the kingdom, the identity of the Thracian successors. Reign years of Comontorius and Cavarus are on no page, so no ruler strip. The Scordisci (Danube) and the Galatians (Asia Minor, Cliopatria's galatia) are the other Celtic settlements of the 279 invasion. The odrysian-kingdom dossier hands Seuthes III's realm to this state; the Odrysian line is said there to continue obscurely, so the land after 212 is left to nobody.
